_meta.title: US financial benchmarks
_meta.inspiredBy: Federal Reserve Survey of Consumer Finances (SCF) 2022 + Fidelity savings-multiple guideposts
_meta.disclaimer: For entertainment and educational purposes only. Not financial advice.
howToUpdate: These are realistic PLACEHOLDER values calibrated to public SCF-style ranges. They are not exact published figures.

netWorthPercentilesByAge models INVESTABLE net worth (savings + investments minus total debt), which is intentionally lower than full SCF net worth because it excludes home equity and other illiquid assets. Our form only collects savings/investments and total debt.

To refresh: pull the latest SCF release (https://www.federalreserve.gov/econres/scfindex.htm), recompute per-age percentile breakpoints for liquid + investment assets net of debt, and replace the anchors below.
savingsMultipleTargets follow the Fidelity-style 'save X times your income by age Y' rule of thumb and can be tuned freely.
All dollar values are in USD. Ages are in years.

scoring._incomeFloorNote: Income-relative ratios (savings-to-income, debt-to-income, net-savings, age-adjusted progress) are computed against max(income, incomeFloor). This prevents an unrealistically low income (e.g. $90) from inflating ratios and producing a higher score than a larger income with identical savings/debt. ~ full-time minimum wage; tune freely.

curves._note: Each curve is a list of [input, score] anchors used for piecewise-linear interpolation. score is 0..1.
